frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui-compatible component primitives
frontend.state: Server Components and server actions for standard flows; client state only for interactive discovery/catalog workflows

backend.framework: Next.js route handlers and server actions
backend.api_style: Route Handler -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma for REST-style JSON endpoints and app-owned mutations
backend.background_jobs: Separate TypeScript BullMQ worker on Redis for all long-running tasks

packages.packages/domain: Domain services, use cases, orchestration, business logic, and service interfaces consumed by web and worker.
packages.packages/ai: AI Capability Router, provider adapter interfaces, provider implementations, request/response normalization, and provider health checks.
packages.packages/scrapers: Playwright website discovery, navigation tree extraction, PDF/OCR import connectors, and raw artifact collection.
packages.packages/shared: Shared utilities, config helpers, logging, errors, constants, and cross-cutting primitives.
packages.packages/validation: Deterministic validation rules, duplicate checks, SKU/price/category rules, and candidate-to-catalog import gates.
packages.packages/types: Shared TypeScript types, DTOs, schemas, queue payloads, and API contracts.

domain_service_layer.request_flow: Route Handler / Server Action -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma -> PostgreSQL
domain_service_layer.worker_flow: BullMQ Processor -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma -> PostgreSQL
domain_service_layer.rule: Business logic lives in domain services and validation package, not directly inside route handlers, server actions, or queue processors.

database.search: PostgreSQL full-text search for MVP; external search deferred until scale evidence exists

storage.usage: PDF uploads, generated PDFs/PNGs, import snapshots, rendered DOM snapshots when retained

authentication.tenant_model: Workspace maps to Clerk organization and application workspace_id
authentication.authorization: Application-enforced RBAC with workspace_owner for MVP

hosting_and_deployment.workers: Fly.io TypeScript worker service with Playwright runtime
hosting_and_deployment.observability: Sentry plus structured logs and queue/job metrics

testing_stack.route_integration: Vitest against route handlers/server actions through domain services
testing_stack.worker_integration: Vitest against BullMQ processors through domain services
testing_stack.security: tenant-isolation integration tests and credential handling checks

ai_and_external_services.status: stable interface for all AI integrations

pipeline_architecture.scraping_pipeline: External source -> connector/scraper -> raw import artifact -> normalized source record -> Discovery Session candidate seed
pipeline_architecture.ai_enrichment_pipeline: Normalized source record or catalog candidate -> AI Capability Router -> Provider Adapter -> enrichment result -> validation -> candidate/catalog update
pipeline_architecture.separation_rule: Scraping collects and normalizes source data; AI enrichment is independently repeatable and can re-enrich stored normalized source records without re-scraping.
pipeline_architecture.re_enrichment_support: Persist normalized source records and import artifacts with version/source hashes so users can rerun enrichment after changing provider, prompt, capability route, or validation rules.

selected_stack.rationale: A Next.js full-stack monorepo with a separate BullMQ worker is the simplest scalable architecture: route handlers and server actions stay thin, all business logic is centralized in shared domain services, workers reuse the same domain services, scraping and AI enrichment remain independent pipelines, and the AI Capability Router/Provider Adapter interface remains stable for all AI integrations.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Too risky for Playwright/OCR/AI jobs; workers must scale and run independently.
Adds a second language while frontend, Playwright, and worker ecosystem remain TypeScript-heavy.
Over-engineered before scale evidence; monorepo packages plus separate worker are enough.
Unnecessary until catalog scale proves PostgreSQL full-text insufficient.

execution_decisions.assumption: Use dependency-aware vertical slices after a thin monorepo, tenant, data, and queue foundation.
execution_decisions.risk_if_false: Feature demonstrations arrive later or require sequence revision.

execution_decisions.assumption: Use milestone exit criteria rather than calendar dates because no launch deadline was approved upstream.
execution_decisions.risk_if_false: Capacity planning will need calendar estimates later.

execution_decisions.assumption: Defer Flyer and Quote builders from the launch package because Stage 1 permits deferral when risk grows and Stage 4 contains no approved UI blueprints for them.
execution_decisions.risk_if_false: The launch package may omit desired secondary business outputs.

execution_decisions.assumption: Release through internal validation, private alpha, controlled beta, then public readiness review.
execution_decisions.risk_if_false: Operational work may be overbuilt for an internal-only launch or insufficient for a public launch.

execution_decisions.assumption: Generated Stage 6 agent profiles use GPT 5.5 and ticket-scoped edit/bash permissions.
execution_decisions.risk_if_false: Agent files require a model or permission-policy update before execution.

risks.risk: Website scraping behavior and anti-bot variability can destabilize the core import slice.
risks.mitigation: Build a narrow representative-site spike first; persist normalized artifacts; use idempotent per-category jobs and manual entry fallback.
risks.next_action: Validate representative sites in TICKET-010 before broadening scraper behavior.

risks.risk: Async job, worker, and UI status contracts may drift across web and worker workstreams.
risks.mitigation: Freeze shared queue payload and job-state contracts in packages/types before parallel UI/worker implementation.
risks.next_action: Review shared contracts at BATCH-002 merge gate.

risks.risk: Tenant isolation or credential handling defects could expose workspace or provider data.
risks.mitigation: Require workspace-scoped repositories, encrypted/server-only credentials, negative tenant tests, and security review before alpha.
risks.next_action: Complete TICKET-003 and TICKET-019 before LAUNCH-GATE-001.

risks.risk: Dense discovery and catalog interfaces may fail keyboard, responsive, or visual continuity requirements.
risks.mitigation: Build shared accessible table/drawer patterns first and require preview, screenshot, keyboard, responsive, and design-system evidence.
risks.next_action: Validate frontend tickets through TICKET-020 before beta.

risks.risk: AI provider behavior and extraction quality vary while zero-provider operation remains mandatory.
risks.mitigation: Keep provider adapters behind capability contracts, use deterministic validation, and test manual-only operation as a release gate.
risks.next_action: Validate configured and zero-provider modes in TICKET-007 and TICKET-020.

ticket_risks.risk: Website scraping behavior and anti-bot variability can destabilize the core import slice.
ticket_risks.mitigation: Build a narrow representative-site spike first; persist normalized artifacts; use idempotent per-category jobs and manual entry fallback.
ticket_risks.next_action: Validate representative sites in TICKET-010 before broadening scraper behavior.

ticket_risks.risk: Async job, worker, and UI status contracts may drift across web and worker workstreams.
ticket_risks.mitigation: Freeze shared queue payload and job-state contracts in packages/types before parallel UI/worker implementation.
ticket_risks.next_action: Review shared contracts at BATCH-002 merge gate.

ticket_risks.risk: Tenant isolation or credential handling defects could expose workspace or provider data.
ticket_risks.mitigation: Require workspace-scoped repositories, encrypted/server-only credentials, negative tenant tests, and security review before alpha.
ticket_risks.next_action: Complete TICKET-003 and TICKET-019 before LAUNCH-GATE-001.

ticket_risks.risk: Dense discovery and catalog interfaces may fail keyboard, responsive, or visual continuity requirements.
ticket_risks.mitigation: Build shared accessible table/drawer patterns first and require preview, screenshot, keyboard, responsive, and design-system evidence.
ticket_risks.next_action: Validate frontend tickets through TICKET-020 before beta.

ticket_risks.risk: AI provider behavior and extraction quality vary while zero-provider operation remains mandatory.
ticket_risks.mitigation: Keep provider adapters behind capability contracts, use deterministic validation, and test manual-only operation as a release gate.
ticket_risks.next_action: Validate configured and zero-provider modes in TICKET-007 and TICKET-020.
